topics.topic: Exact public export surface of data_provider, including the three omitted constants
questions: Must `VIEWER_ENTRY_CLIENT_IDENTITY_MAX_CHARACTERS` and `VIEWER_ENTRY_CLIENT_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN` be added to the public capabilities, despite their absence from the Candidate public capabilities list?
Must `REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT`, required by A6 and A30 to form `projects/active`, be added to the public capabilities, or is it intentionally not exported?

Are REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT, VIEWER_ENTRY_CLIENT_IDENTITY_MAX_CHARACTERS and VIEWER_ENTRY_CLIENT_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN public exports even though they are absent from Candidate public capabilities, and is that capability list exhaustive?

Which list defines the exact public export surface: the closure named in Owns or the Candidate public capabilities block, which omits `VIEWER_ENTRY_CLIENT_IDENTITY_MAX_CHARACTERS`, `VIEWER_ENTRY_CLIENT_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN`, and `REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT` even though A25 and A6 name them as data-provider constants?

quotes:
The typed constants of `70_data_provider_closure.json`, the one home of each
value generated code reads (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10 version 2, 15.3.1): the money
values and work-balance signs (A9), the Registry paths and timeout
(A6, A30), the session lifetimes and credential entropy (A30), the audit
significance (A13), the capability sets (A2), the staff and principal
transitions (A3), the password bounds (A16), the supported contract versions
(A7), the import audit table (A18), the completion bound (A20), the transport
values (A25, among them the viewer-entry client identity bound and its
`unknown` stand-in since 2026-11-10) and the bootstrap exit codes (A29). The
list names groups; every constant of that closure is exported.

Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): the values the generated transport guard and runtime read are data-provider constants: `API_PREFIX`, `VIEWER_ENTRY_PATH`, `VIEWER_LOGOUT_PATH`, `NO_STORE_PATHS`, `NO_STORE_CACHE_CONTROL`, `SECURITY_HEADERS`, `TRANSPORT_LOG_LABELS`, `HEALTH_LIVE_PATH`, `HEALTH_READY_PATH`, `HEALTH_OK_STATUS`, and `TRANSPORT_GUARD_STATUSES`, the status of each refusal of the guard keyed by `= models.TransportGuardRefusal`. The client network identity of the viewer-entry limiter is bounded by `VIEWER_ENTRY_CLIENT_IDENTITY_MAX_CHARACTERS` (its leading characters kept) and stands in as `VIEWER_ENTRY_CLIENT_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN` when the connection names no client; the notes of `transport_guard` state the bound and the source (owner-approved cleanup 2026-11-10: lost from the notes since `018b2e2e`; the leaves `maximum_characters` and `unknown_placeholder` of `limits.viewer_entry.client_network_identity` leave the policy). Their former leaves (`public_api_prefix`, `security_headers`, `browser_session.logout_path`, `health.liveness_path`, `health.readiness_path`) leave the policy; the cookie name and attributes stay, the viewer cookie backend reads them.

Each value reaches code by one path of SPEC_STANDARD 15.3.1. A deployment value is a row of `config.runtime_environment_variables` read only by `load_runtime_settings`, into a field of `RuntimeSettings` (`database_url`, `environment`, `public_origin`, `trusted_hosts`, `allowed_origins`, `max_request_body_bytes`, `max_binary_response_bytes`, `production_logging`, the two viewer-entry limits and, since 2026-11-09, `registry_base_url`, `binary_storage_root` and `binary_max_read_bytes`); the emitted `binary_storage` reads the last two from the settings `load_runtime_settings` returns, like every other reader. A release value is a data-provider constant generated code imports (below). The storage table names of `config.persistence` are read only by the emitted repositories, through the persistence backend IR; `config.credential_hash_scheme` only by the emitted `credential_security`. No model-written note names a `config` address. Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): the Registry request paths and timeout, the staff and viewer session lifetimes and the credential entropy have the same value in every environment and change only by a decision about the product, so by SPEC_STANDARD 15.2 (check 4 before 3) they are data-provider constants that generated code imports (`REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH`, `REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT` (Q12), `REGISTRY_CONTEXT_SEGMENT`, `REGISTRY_VALIDATE_SEGMENT`, `REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `STAFF_SESSION_TTL_HOURS`, `VIEWER_SESSION_TTL_DAYS`, `CREDENTIAL_SECRET_BYTES`), values unchanged; the path templates are split into a path and three segments (the active one added by Q12), because a template is not data (15.11). The Registry URL itself is an environment value: since the owner's decision of 2026-11-09 it is the `registry_base_url` field of `RuntimeSettings`, a required row of the start-up table, and the data-provider constant `REGISTRY_BASE_URL_VARIABLE` that named the variable for the gateway is removed (SPEC_STANDARD 6.11).
judgement.why: The Owns passage makes every closure constant an export, and State 2 expressly identifies all three omitted names as data-provider constants; the block is labeled candidate rather than exhaustive.

topics.topic: Exact minimal set of models symbols that data_provider may depend on
questions: Replace the generic dependency with the exact minimal list of model, enum, and interface symbols that `data_provider` directly names, constructs, checks, or uses in annotations.
Which exact model, enum and interface symbols may data_provider import from models?
Replace the module-wide description with the exact minimal list of models-owned row models, enums and interfaces that data_provider directly names, constructs or checks.

quotes:
Each module's `Knows` section names exactly the modules it imports (the
`imports.module_internal` the imports closure projects, which since
2026-11-08 carries the edge `api` → `api_irregular` of the running code as
well). Lines of the list are layers, not an
assertion that every module imports every earlier one. `Knows` is the
module-level edge only: which symbols a consumer imports from each provider
is the imports closure (`65_imports.json`, projected into
`imports.module_internal`, SPEC_STANDARD §7), the one authoritative
consumer → provider → symbols map.
`models`, for the row models and enumerations of its tables.
judgement.why: The text expressly limits Knows to the module-level edge and assigns the exact minimal symbol surface to the authoritative imports closure, so the generic Knows wording is not the module_internal symbol list governed by §7.
